newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent eases as "clockings" confirm weak tone.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent eases as "clockings" confirm weak tone.

text.p: Dated Brent eased on Monday as demand for February barrels ebbed but other North Sea grades were notionally unchanged in thin talk, traders said.
Brent due to load Feb 16-18 traded between majors at March Brent +29 cents a barrel, four cents cheaper than on Friday.
The benchmark crude came under further pressure later in the day when two cargoes, due to load Feb 18-20, went unclaimed at the five o'clock deadline.
The cargoes were "clocked" to Nova and JP Morgan, who kept a Feb 17-19 cargo on Friday and was clocked with a second.
"There's a lack of interest. There is no need for the crude, and we are a couple of weeks away from the March programmes. It's going to be quiet until IP week," a trader said.
Softer sentiment was reflected in the paper market, where Feb/Mar slid about 15 cents to fetch +47 cents while Mar/Apr traded twice at Mar +43 cents, down from +45 late on Friday.
Brent CFDs slipped about eight cents to March +23/+30 for Feb 3-7 dates, and five cents to March +10/+11 for Feb 10-14.
"The market was looking top-heavy," one trader said.
Other North Sea markets were slow, with remaining February supply thin and most refiners covered, but a Flotta loading Feb 20-22 traded at Dated Brent -49 cents, slightly up on last done.

Two or three small Urals cargoes due to load before February 20 were putting pressure on spot market differentials in the Mediterranean, where refiners were still contemplating cutting runs due to poor margins, traders said.
Talk of a deal Friday at Dated -75 cents a barrel cif Genoa was denied but even potential sellers said it would be difficult to achieve that level this week.
